KP 1. Calculating an Amount of Money After Compound Interest Is Applied
1.?

A principal of $102,000 is invested in the stock market and earns interest at a rate of 2% per year, compounded daily. To the nearest dollar, how much will the investment with worth after 7 years (ignore the leap years)?

E
Wed, Jul 29th @ 5:53 PM|Elapsed: 1:03Correct

The compound interest equation states that P=P0(1+rn)nt.

The annual interest is compounded daily, and there are 365 days in one year, so n=365. We also have an initial amount of P0=102,000, an annual interest of r=0.02, and a length of t=7 years. Substituting these values into the formula, we obtain

P=P0(1+rn)nt=102,000(1+0.02365)365(7)=102,000(1+0.000054…)2,555=102,000(1.000054…)2,555=102,000(1.150…)≈117,327.

Hence, after 7 years, the value will be $117,327.

2.?

Mike has deposited $5,000 into an account paying 1% annual interest, compounded monthly. How much money will be in his account after 15 years? Round your answer to the nearest dollar.

E
Wed, Jul 29th @ 5:55 PM|Elapsed: 1:04Correct

The compound interest equation states that P=P0(1+rn)nt.

The annual interest is compounded monthly, and there are 12 months in one year, so n=12. We also have an initial amount of P0=5,000, an annual interest of r=0.01, and a length of t=15 years. Substituting these values into the formula, we obtain

P=P0(1+rn)nt=5,000(1+0.0112)12(15)=5,000(1+0.000833…)180=5,000(1.000833…)180=5,000(1.16176…)≈5,809.

Hence, after 15 years, Mike will have $5,809 in the account.

3.?

How much money would you need to deposit today at a 10% annual interest rate, compounded yearly, to have $40,000 in the account after 20 years? Round your answer to the nearest dollar.

The annual interest is compounded once per year, so we have n=1. We also have an annual rate of r=0.1, and a final amount of P=40,000 after t=20 years. To find the initial deposit, P0, we substitute these values into the formula and solve for P0:

P=P0(1+rn)nt40,000=P0(1+0.11)1(20)40,000=P0(1.1)2040,000=P0(6.727…)P0=40,0006.727…P0≈5,946

Consequently, you would need to deposit $5,946.

P=P0(1+rn)nt37,500=P0(1+0.03365)365(6)37,500=P0(1.000082…)2,19037,500=P0(1.197…)P0=37,5001.197…P0≈31,323

KP 3. Calculating the Number of Years to Yield a Particular Amount
5.?

If you deposit $2,000 into an account with a 20% annual interest rate, compounded semi-annually, how many years will it take until there is at least $4,000 in the account?

H
Wed, Jul 29th @ 6:24 PM|Elapsed: 3:22Correct

The compound interest equation states that P=P0(1+rn)nt.

The annual interest is compounded semi-annually, so n=2. We also have an initial amount of P0=2,000 and annual rate of r=0.2.

To find the number of years it will take until P≥4,000, we substitute these values into the formula and solve for t:

P=P0(1+rn)nt≥4,0002,000(1+0.22)2t≥4,000(1+0.1)2t≥4,0002,000(1.1)2t≥2log⁡(1.12t)≥log⁡(2)2tlog⁡(1.1)≥log⁡(2)2t≥log⁡(2)log⁡(1.1)2t≥7.272…t≥7.272…2≈3.64

Remember payments are compounded semi-annually, so we must choose either 3.5 or 4 years.

  • After 3.5 years, there is still less than $4,000 in the account, because 3.5<3.64.

  • After 4 years, there will be more than $4,000 in the account, since 4>3.64.

Therefore, it will take 4 years until there is at least $4,000 in the account.

6.?

If you deposit $12,000 into an account with a 8% annual interest rate, compounded quarterly, how many years will it take until there is at least $18,000 in the account?

H
Wed, Jul 29th @ 6:26 PM|Elapsed: 1:55Correct

The compound interest equation states that P=P0(1+rn)nt.

The annual interest is compounded quarterly, and there are 4 quarters in one year, so n=4. We also have an initial amount of P0=12,000 and annual rate of r=0.08.

To find the number of years it will take until P≥18,000, we substitute these values into the formula and solve for t:

P=P0(1+rn)nt≥18,00012,000(1+0.084)4t≥18,000(1+0.02)4t≥18,00012,000(1.02)4t≥1.5log(1.024t)≥log(1.5)4tlog(1.02)≥log(1.5)4t≥log(1.5)log(1.02)4t≥20.475…t≥20.475…4≈5.12

Remember, payments are compounded quarterly, so we must choose either 5 or 5.25 years.

  • After 5 years, there is still less than $18,000 in the account, because 5<5.12.

  • After 5.25 years, there will be more than $18,000 in the account, since 5.25>5.12.

Therefore, it will take 5.25 years (5 years and 1 quarter) until there is at least $18,000 in the account.
